items.q: Was Bun's $165K AI rewrite bill a scandal?
items.a: Primeagen calls it a **steal**. The Zig→Rust port took **11 days**, ~**6,502 commits**, ~**1.8M lines**, and ~**$165K** in API spend — vs his Netflix rewrite of **3 engineers × ~1 year → >$1M** fully loaded plus feature freeze.

items.q: Why can cost, quality, and speed all improve together here?
items.a: Even if AI output is only ~**50% of desired shape** and three engineers spend three months cleaning up, the port still beats a pure human rewrite on the **cost / quality / speed** triangle — "one of the rare three-point triangle W's."

items.q: What bug class drove the Bun rewrite?
items.a: Bun's Zig codebase accumulated **use-after-free, leaks, double-free, and races** from mixing **GC with manual memory**. Jared frames that mix — not Zig itself — as the unusual risk.

items.q: Why prefer Rust compiler rules over style guides?
items.a: Tiger Style and Google C++ guides are **best-effort social contracts**. Rust makes ownership a **compile error** via RAII/drop — stronger than Zig `defer` or review/linters at Bun's scale (~**20%** was already C++ with the same enforcement gap).

items.q: What was the translation → review loop?
items.a: **File-by-file Zig→Rust mechanical translation**, then **two fresh-context reviewer agents**, then apply feedback. Primeagen maps this to **Prime Agent Review**, where about **50% of feedback is actually good**.

items.q: How did they burn down ~16K compile errors?
items.a: Many **Claude Code workers in git worktrees**, each fixing **one error or test slice**, looping until compile errors and then **unit-test shards** went green.

items.q: Is compile-green enough to ship a rewrite?
items.a: No. First `bun --version` still **linker-panicked**. The real confidence gate was the **unit-test fleet**, not a green compile alone. Mechanical translation ≠ idiomatic Rust — expect heavy cleanup.

sections.title: What AI is actually good at

items.q: What does Primeagen think LLMs are unusually strong at?
items.a: **Mechanical translation** — "translating one thing to the next thing." Language choice used to be a **one-way decision** for a project like Bun; agent fleets collapsed that assumption in weeks.
